claims.excerpt: Why the 1906 Earthquake Has Different Magnitude Estimates
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: The supplied evidence gives estimates of 7.7 and 7.9 using different methods.
claims.synthesisStatement: Different methods of estimating earthquake size can disagree.
claims.narrativeStatement: Why the 1906 earthquake has different magnitude estimates
claims.explanation: Faithfully frames the contrast established by the two estimates.

claims.excerpt: One team studied seismic recordings from 96 observatories, then digitized and modeled usable data from 12.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: Records were available from 96 observatories; 12 stations had records suitable for digitization and modeling.
claims.synthesisStatement: One team studied seismic recordings from 96 observatories and digitized and modeled usable data from 12.
claims.narrativeStatement: One team studied seismic recordings from 96 observatories and digitized and modeled usable data from 12.
claims.explanation: Preserves the observatory count and the qualified count of usable records.

claims.excerpt: Its analysis suggested a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: The seismic results suggested surface-wave magnitude 7.7.
claims.synthesisStatement: That seismic analysis suggested a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7.
claims.narrativeStatement: That seismic analysis suggested a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7.
claims.explanation: Preserves both the tentative attribution and the surface-wave scale.

claims.excerpt: A USGS team took a different approach, re-evaluating geodetic measurements made before and after the earthquake.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: USGS re-evaluated geodetic measurements from before and after the event.
claims.synthesisStatement: A USGS team instead re-evaluated geodetic measurements made before and after the earthquake.
claims.narrativeStatement: A USGS team instead re-evaluated geodetic measurements made before and after the earthquake.
claims.explanation: Faithfully states the team, method, and timing of the measurements.

claims.excerpt: Those measurements captured ground deformation through angles and distances between benchmarks, producing an estimate of 7.9.
claims.label: F1
claims.sourceEvidence: USGS assessed deformation using benchmark distances and angles; its slip models suggested moment magnitude 7.9.
claims.synthesisStatement: The geodetic approach used ground deformation reflected in angles and distances between benchmarks and gave an estimate of 7.9.
claims.narrativeStatement: The geodetic approach used ground deformation reflected in angles and distances between benchmarks and gave an estimate of 7.9.
claims.explanation: The core method and estimate are preserved, but the article inherits the synthesis's omission that 7.9 was moment magnitude suggested by slip models. The wording also compresses the role of the models into the measurements 'producing' the estimate.

claims.excerpt: The two estimates differ because they come from different methods of assessing earthquake size.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: The supplied evidence says the methods estimate earthquake size differently and can produce differing estimates.
claims.synthesisStatement: Different methods of estimating earthquake size can disagree.
claims.narrativeStatement: Different methods of estimating earthquake size can disagree.
claims.explanation: Applies the supported general takeaway to the two estimates described above.

steps: Describes its measurement basis and gives its estimate.
Connects the difference to the use of different methods.

redundancy: The title and final sentence both state that the earthquake has differing estimates because different methods were used.
